question: What is the primary difference between original Universal Precautions and modern Standard Precautions?

options.A: Standard Precautions apply only to surgical wards
options.B: Universal Precautions apply exclusively to airborne pathogens
options.C: Universal Precautions require the mandatory use of respirators for all patients
options.D: Standard Precautions include all body fluids and moist secretions

explanation: While original Universal Precautions focused specifically on blood and blood-contaminated fluids, Standard Precautions expanded coverage to include all body fluids, non-intact skin, and mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why do healthcare professionals treat all patients as potentially infectious under Standard Precautions?

options.A: Laboratory diagnostic tests are too expensive for routine use
options.B: Patients prefer knowing that strict barriers are being utilized
options.C: Infected individuals can be asymptomatic and unaware of their status
options.D: Hospital management mandates this to conserve cleaning supplies

explanation: Many patients carrying bloodborne or other pathogens show no outward symptoms, making universal barrier use essential to prevent silent transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: A nurse working in a rural clinic experiences a temporary interruption in running water. What is the most appropriate immediate action for hand hygiene compliance?

options.A: Perform hand hygiene using dry tissue paper instead of washing
options.B: Postpone all nursing procedures until municipal water supply is restored
options.C: Use alcohol-based hand rub or stored clean water with soap via alternative dispensers
options.D: Proceed with patient care while wearing sterile gloves without washing hands

explanation: When running water fails, alternative dispensing methods like stored water systems or alcohol-based hand rubs ensure hand hygiene protocols are maintained. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is NOT an acceptable response to resource shortages regarding Personal Protective Equipment?

options.A: Using alternative dispensing methods for handwashing water
options.B: Procuring emergency stocks through hospital administrative channels
options.C: Reusing single-use disposable gloves between multiple different patients
options.D: Prioritizing PPE usage for high-risk invasive procedures

explanation: Disposable gloves are single-use items; reusing them across different patients crosses contamination barriers and spreads pathogens rapidly. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the primary reason for removing gloves first during the PPE doffing sequence?

options.A: Gloves typically carry the highest microbial and fluid contamination load
options.B: Removing gloves allows the nurse to breathe more comfortably
options.C: Gloves are the cheapest items of protective equipment
options.D: Gowns cannot be unfastened while wearing tight gloves

explanation: Because gloves touch patients and contaminated surfaces directly, removing them first prevents accidental transfer of pathogens to other parts of the body or clothing during doffing. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing to assist a physician with an incision and drainage of a deep, abscessed wound that is expected to spray purulent material. Which combination of PPE is most appropriate?

options.A: Surgical mask, clean gloves, and a hair net
options.B: N95 respirator and sterile gloves only
options.C: Gown, surgical mask, eye protection, and gloves
options.D: Sterile gloves and an apron only

explanation: Procedures likely to generate splashes of body fluids require full barrier protection including a gown, mask, eye protection, and gloves to protect skin, mucous membranes, and clothing. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h3)

question: When is handwashing with soap and water strictly preferred over alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: At the beginning and end of an eight-hour nursing shift
options.B: Whenever working in a busy emergency department
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with organic material or blood

explanation: Organic matter and blood physical impede alcohol-based rubs; physical washing with soap and water is required to remove visible soil. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h4)

question: According to the World Health Organization, what is the second moment for hand hygiene?
explanation: The second moment requires hand hygiene immediately before performing clean or aseptic tasks to prevent introducing pathogens into vulnerable patient sites. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the recommended safe method for handling a used hypodermic needle if recapping is unavoidable?

options.A: Bend the needle with forceps before placing it on a tray
options.B: Pass the unsheathed needle to a colleague for disposal
options.C: Use a one-handed scoop technique to guide the needle into the cap
options.D: Hold the cap with the opposite hand and push the needle firmly inward

explanation: The one-handed scoop technique prevents the non-dominant hand from being accidentally punctured during the recapping process. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h5)

question: At what fill level should a designated sharps container be securely closed and replaced?

options.A: When it reaches the three-quarters full line
options.B: When it is completely full to the brim
options.C: Whenever the container starts to feel heavy
options.D: At the end of every weekly ward shift

explanation: Sharps containers should never be overfilled; sealing them at the three-quarters mark prevents accidental punctures from protruding needles. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h5)

question: How should a nurse manage a fresh, large puddle of spilled blood on a clinic floor?

options.A: Pour hot water over the spill and leave it to evaporate naturally
options.B: Call the maintenance department and leave the room unlocked until they arrive
options.C: Sweep the blood away immediately using a dry broom and dustpan
options.D: Cover the spill with absorbent material, apply a chlorine-based disinfectant, and wipe after contact time

explanation: Blood spills must be absorbed first, then disinfected with an appropriate chlorine solution like sodium hypochlorite to inactive bloodborne viruses safely. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which waste stream is typically designated for general, non-hazardous administrative rubbish and food waste in a hospital?
explanation: General municipal-type waste that has no contact with infectious body fluids is discarded in black bins or bags. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h6)

question: A nurse sustains a deep needle-stick injury from a patient known to be living with HIV. What is the immediate first-aid action the nurse should take?

options.A: Apply a tourniquet above the injury site to trap circulating pathogens
options.B: Cover the wound tightly with an adhesive bandage and continue the shift
options.C: Apply strong concentrated bleach directly into the wound puncture
options.D: Wash the puncture site immediately with soap and running water without aggressive squeezing

explanation: Washing with soap and water cleans the wound without damaging local tissues or driving pathogens deeper through milking or squeezing. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h7)

question: Within what maximum time window must Post-Exposure Prophylaxis for HIV ideally be initiated after a high-risk exposure?
explanation: PEP is most effective when started immediately and must be initiated within 72 hours of exposure to prevent viral replication and seroconversion. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h7)

question: How can a community health nurse best assist a family caring for a relative with a chronic draining wound at home?

options.A: Instruct them to burn all soiled dressings in an open backyard fire
options.B: Require the family to purchase hospital-grade biohazard bins for their kitchen
options.C: Advise them to stop changing dressings until a doctor visits the home
options.D: Provide education on hand hygiene, safe dressing disposal, and improvised barrier use

explanation: Community education equips home caregivers with practical skills to manage waste and maintain hygiene safely without complex clinical infrastructure. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h8)

question: What is a primary infection control challenge unique to home-based care compared to hospital environments?

options.B: Limited access to formal medical waste disposal infrastructure
options.C: Mandatory air filtration systems in every household
options.D: Constant supervision by occupational health physicians

explanation: Home care settings lack commercial incinerators and regulated waste disposal streams, requiring community nurses to teach safe alternative containment. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h8)
